result:
Rain taps against the window like a language just beyond translation—persistent, gentle, urgent. I’ve always loved storms, not for their drama, but for the quiet they carve out of chaos. In the hush between thunderclaps, the world seems to exhale, offering a rare permission: *pause*.  

Lately, life has felt like scrolling through a highlight reel of other people’s certainties while my own path flickers with questions. “What’s next?” “Am I enough?” “Why does time move faster the more I try to hold it?” But rain doesn’t ask these things. It simply falls, pooling in cracks, nourishing roots, washing dust from leaves. It reminds me that not all movement is forward—sometimes it’s downward, inward, a slow seep into the soil of your own becoming.  

I think about resilience. Not the loud, triumphant kind, but the quiet endurance of moss on stone or a single weed pushing through concrete. We’re taught to chase brilliance, but maybe the real magic is in persistence—the daily choice to show up, even when the sky is gray and your coffee’s gone cold.  

The storm will pass. The sun will return, harsh and demanding. But for now, in this cocoon of drumming rain, I’m learning to be still. To trust that growth isn’t always visible. That sometimes, the bravest thing you can do is sit with your own uncertainty and listen.  

Outside, the streetlights blink on, casting long, liquid reflections. Inside, I breathe. And for this moment, it’s enough.
